quiz_item.scenario_prompt: While observing insects in the field for Insect Study Requirement 1, what morphological traits distinguish true insects (Class Insecta) from spiders and ticks (Class Arachnida), and how should you treat a honeybee sting?
quiz_item.question: While observing insects in the field for Insect Study Requirement 1, what morphological traits distinguish true insects (Class Insecta) from spiders and ticks (Class Arachnida), and how should you treat a honeybee sting?
options: A. Adult insects have two body regions, eight legs, and no antennae; if stung by a honeybee, squeeze the venom sac firmly between tweezers to inject the remaining venom.
B. Insects and spiders both have internal vertebrate backbones and six wings; bee stings should be treated by applying a tourniquet above the knee.
C. Spiders have three body segments and compound eyes with antennae, whereas insects have a cephalothorax and abdomen with eight legs.

D. Adult insects have three body regions (head, thorax, abdomen), three pairs of jointed legs (six total), one pair of antennae, and usually one or two pairs of wings (unlike eight-legged arachnids); scrape a honeybee stinger out sideways with a flat edge, wash the site, apply a cold pack, and watch closely for signs of anaphylaxis.

Step 2 (Life Cycles): When you embark on your insect safari, prepare a trip plan, or at the very least, tell an adult where you are going (p. 35).
Step 3 (Life Cycles): It is also a good idea to take a friend with you. 2 (p. 35).
Step 4 (Life Cycles): It is a good idea to wear long pants, a long-sleeved shirt, ahat, and closed shoes to keep ticks, chiggers, and insects from biting you or hitching (p. 35).

Step 3 (Insects and People): Plant protection entomologists study insect pests and figure out ways to protect crops, trees, flowers, and other plants from attack and injury (p. 75).
Step 4 (Insects and People): Others work outside, gathering pollen and nectar to provide the raw material for the colony's food (p. 75).
